chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Amr ibn Qays! Are you aware that God, Mighty and Majestic, sent a Messenger and revealed to him a Book, and revealed in the Book everything that is needed, and made for it a guide pointing towards it, and made a limit (hadd) for everything, and for whoever exceeds the limit, a penalty (hadd)?'

He (the narrator) said: I said, 'He sent a Messenger and revealed to him a Book, and revealed in the Book everything that is needed, and made for it a guide, and made a limit for everything.' He said: 'Yes.'

I said, 'And how did He make a penalty for whoever exceeds the limit?' He said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has set a limit concerning wealth: that it cannot be taken except through its permissible means. So whoever takes it through other than its permissible means, his hand is cut off as a penalty for transgressing the limit. And God, Mighty and Majestic, has set a limit that marriage must not be contracted except through its permissible means, and whoever does otherwise — if he is unmarried, he receives the hadd penalty, and if he is married, he is stoned — for transgressing the limit.'

key_terms.حَدّ: Hadd — both 'limit/boundary' (Allah's divine limit) and 'hadd penalty' (a prescribed legal punishment for violating that limit). The dual meaning is deliberate.
key_terms.حِلّ: Permissible means / lawful channel — the licit path through which an action is permitted
key_terms.دَلِيل: Guide/evidence — in this context refers to the Imam as the authoritative guide to the Book
key_terms.عَزَب: Azab — an unmarried person, whose penalty for zina is flogging (jald)
key_terms.مُحْصَن: Muhsan — a person in a valid marriage, whose penalty for zina is stoning (rajm)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about divine limits (hudud) and their penalties in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches Amr ibn Qays the principle that divine law is comprehensive: God sent a complete revelation with a guide (the Imam), established limits (hudud) for everything, and set enforceable penalties for those who transgress these limits. The hadith illustrates this principle with two concrete examples from Islamic penal law (hudud): amputation of the hand for unlawful acquisition of property (theft), and flogging or stoning for unlawful sexual intercourse (zina). This teaching reflects the Shia theological position on the completeness of divine guidance through Quran, Prophet, and Imam.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, fromMuhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Ibn Dubays Al Kufy, from Amro Bin Qays who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘O Amro Bin Qays! Are you aware that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Sent a Rasoolsaww and Revealed unto himsaww a Book, and Revealed in the Book everything what is needed to it, and Made for it an evidence pointing towards it, and Made a Limit (Hadd) for everything, and for the one who exceeds the Limit (Hadd), (there is) a Penalty (Hadd)?’

I said, ‘Heazwj Sent a Rasoolsaww and Revealed unto himsaww a Book, and Revealed in the Book everything what is needed to it, and Made for it an evidence pointing towards it, and Made a Limit (Hadd) for everything, and for the one who exceeds the Limit (Hadd), (there is) a Penalty (Hadd)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.

I said, ‘And how did Heazwj Make a Penalty (Hadd) to be upon the one who exceeds the Limit (Hadd)?’ Heasws said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has a Limit (Hadd) in the wealth and that you cannot take it except from its Permissible means. So the one who takes if from others than its Permissible means, his hands are cut, being a Penalty (Hadd) for exceeding the Limit (Hadd). And that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has a Penalty (Hadd) that you should not copulate with the copulation except by its Permissible means, and the one who does other than that, if he is a celibate, is a Penalty (Hadd), and if he was married, stoning, for having exceeded the Penalty (Hadd)’.
